entries.title: Live-eval retry economics: a severed CORE run retries from SCRATCH (~110 min, ~$70/attempt); client timeout below server runtime guarantees fail-and-retry; a completed-but-unlistened run's bundle is unrecoverable

A fourth attempt auto-spawned (timeout 100min < runtime 113min = guaranteed fail) and was killed manually. Fix direction: (a) persist the finished bundle server-side keyed by an idempotency/request id so a reconnecting client can fetch it (the run is request-bound today — ARCH_ESCALATION 'checkpoint/resume' trigger territory, but bundle-persistence alone is a small slice); (b) eval harness: default IMPORT_EVAL_TIMEOUT_MS must exceed observed CORE runtime (150min), and full-run retries should be OPT-IN for wave gates (a retry restarts a $70 run).
entries.fixture: none yet — server test: unifiedImport persists the bundle on completion; eval test: retry policy honors a max-attempts env
entries.lesson: For long-running jobs, the retry unit must be cheaper than the job — otherwise a retry is a bill, not a recovery. And a result computed with nobody listening must be persisted, not discarded.
